The '''1971–72 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|69th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|40th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

== Summary ==
During summer President [[Santiago Bernabéu (footballer)|Santiago Bernabéu]] transferred out several players such as Sanchis, Bueno, Planelles, Gento (retired), Betancort, Calpe, De La Fuente, Jimenez, Espíldora and Fermín. The club new arrivals were goalkeeper García Remón and a teenage 19-yrs-old forward Santillana in a sign of rejuvenate the squad and a reduced transfers budget for the upcoming years.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=as.com|title=The Dilemma of Real Madrid in 1971|url=http://www.as.com/static/pdf/ascolor/03/numero3_ok.pdf|access-date=7 June 2020}}</ref>

The club won its 15th League title<ref>For this campaign [[La Liga|Primera División]] championship format was expanded from 15 to 17 teams competing and from 30 to 34 rounds</ref> two points above Defending Champions [[Valencia CF]] after a 0–0 draw of [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]]<ref>According to Eduardo Campanero, Honorary President (Chairman) of [[Córdoba CF]], Real Madrid offered 100,000 pesetas (Spanish currency) for each Córdoba player to not let Barcelona (then in 2nd place of the League table) win the match. {{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20141219/fc-barcelona/hubo-prima-del-madrid-al-cordoba_54421977575.html|work=Mundo Deportivo|title=There Had Money from Madrid to Córdoba}}</ref> against Córdoba CF at Los Carmenes one round before season finale.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/12/18/futbol/equipos/cordoba/1418907977.html|title=The Day when Real Madrid pay Córdoba to not let Barcelona win a Match|publisher=Diario Marca|date=18 December 2014|access-date=1 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref> The team played the [[UEFA Cup]] for the first time and was early eliminated in Eightfinals by Dutch side [[PSV Eindhoven]] due to away goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0237-0e9661614251-7a6a4dd29903-1000--why-a-3-1-lead-is-dangerous-for-real-madrid/|title=Why a 3–1 is dangerous for Real Madrid?|publisher=UEFA}}</ref> During June, the squad reached the [[1971–72 Copa del Generalísimo]] semi-finals being defeated by [[Valencia CF]] lost 1–0 at Mestalla and a draw 0–0 in Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/archivo/fotos/el-equipo-del-valencia-club-de-futbol-que-paso-a-la-final-de-la-4963170.html|title=Valencia advanced to the Copa del Generalísimo Final|work=ABC|location=Spain|language=Spanish|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref>
